content: 1. Administer 20 mg of the medication orally once daily for 4 weeks. If symptoms persist after the initial 4 weeks, consider extending treatment for an additional 4 weeks. 2. For a treatment duration of 4 to 8 weeks, administer 20-40 mg orally once daily. 3. If oral therapy is not feasible, administer 20-40 mg intravenously once daily for up to 10 days. Transition to oral administration as soon as the patient can swallow. 4. For maintenance therapy, administer 20 mg orally once daily for up to 6 months. 5. For eradication of Helicobacter pylori in patients with duodenal ulcers, administer 40 mg orally once daily for 10 days, combined with amoxicillin 1000 mg orally every 12 hours for 10 days, and clarithromycin 500 mg orally every 12 hours for 10 days. 6. For risk reduction of rebleeding in gastric or duodenal ulcers following therapeutic endoscopy in adults, administer an initial dose of 80 mg intravenously over 30 minutes, followed by a continuous intravenous infusion of 8 mg/hour for a total treatment duration of 72 hours. Follow this with oral acid-suppressive therapy. 7. For over-the-counter use, administer 20 mg orally once daily for 14 days. 8. Esomeprazole is contraindicated for use with erlotinib due to a reduction in erlotinib levels caused by altered gastric pH, which decreases its solubility and bioavailability. Avoid concomitant use of proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) with erlotinib. 9. Esomeprazole increases the levels of mavacamten by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated as it may lead to heart failure due to systolic dysfunction. 10. Esomeprazole decreases the levels of nelfinavir through mechanisms involving CYP2C19 inhibition and reduced gastric pH, leading to decreased absorption and loss of virologic response. This interaction is contraindicated. 11. Esomeprazole decreases the levels of rilpivirine by increasing gastric pH, which may result in treatment failure and resistance. This interaction is contraindicated. 12. Esomeprazole decreases the levels of acalabrutinib by increasing gastric pH, reducing its solubility. Avoid or use an alternative drug, as separating doses may not eliminate the interaction due to the prolonged effect of PPIs. 13. Apalutamide decreases the levels of esomeprazole by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug, as this interaction may reduce the efficacy of esomeprazole. 14. Esomeprazole decreases the levels of atazanavir by increasing gastric pH, which reduces its solubility. Avoid or use an alternative drug, as substantial reductions in atazanavir plasma concentrations are expected. 15. Carbamazepine decreases the levels of esomeprazole by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 16. Esomeprazole decreases the levels of itraconazole and ketoconazole by increasing gastric pH, which reduces their solubility. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 17. Esomeprazole increases the toxicity of cilostazol by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Reduce the cilostazol dose by 50%. 18. Esomeprazole decreases the efficacy of clopidogrel by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism, which is necessary for clopidogrel activation. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 19. Esomeprazole decreases the levels of dasatinib, pazopanib, and nilotinib by increasing gastric pH, which reduces their solubility. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 20. Esomeprazole increases the levels of digoxin by increasing gastric pH. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Esomeprazole decreases the levels of mesalamine by increasing gastric pH, which affects the dissolution of sustained-release formulations. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 22. Esomeprazole decreases the levels of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by increasing gastric pH, which reduces velpatasvir solubility. Avoid coadministration or administer sofosbuvir/velpatasvir with food 4 hours before esomeprazole. 23. Esomeprazole decreases the levels of sotorasib by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 24. Esomeprazole increases the levels of amitriptyline by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Esomeprazole decreases the levels of amphetamine by increasing gastric pH, which reduces its absorption. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Esomeprazole increases the levels of cannabidiol by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Monitor closely and consider dose adjustments. 27. Esomeprazole decreases the levels of belumosudil by increasing gastric pH. Increase the belumosudil dosage to 200 mg twice daily when coadministered with PPIs. 28. Esomeprazole decreases the levels of bosutinib by increasing gastric pH, which affects its solubility. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 29. Esomeprazole decreases the levels of budesonide by increasing gastric pH, which may cause premature dissolution of extended-release formulations. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 30. Esomeprazole decreases the levels of bendamustine by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Esomeprazole increases the levels of bortezomib by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Esomeprazole decreases the levels of bosentan by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Esomeprazole decreases the levels of sparsentan by increasing gastric pH, which reduces its solubility. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 34. Esomeprazole increases the levels of axitinib by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Esomeprazole decreases the levels of belzutifan by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 36. Esomeprazole decreases the levels of neratinib by increasing gastric pH, which reduces its solubility. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 37. Esomeprazole decreases the levels of tucatinib by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 38. Esomeprazole decreases the levels of pexidartinib by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 39. Esomeprazole decreases the levels of phenobarbital by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Esomeprazole decreases the levels of ampicillin by increasing gastric pH, which reduces its solubility. Use caution and monitor closely.
